items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: And how I got the gig was they went to California... Cab Calloway had to come back east without a bass player... Cab says, 'Can I have him?' So Zutty says, 'Yeah you can have him' and nobody asked me nothing. So they just gave me to Cab.

ctx.x: Yes. We, those musicians, I see pictures sometimes with them. And then you got the job with Cab Calloway and started traveling.
Oh, yeah, 1935. Cab had a great bass player and the most magnificent man I’ve ever seen.

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was in Cab Calloway‟s band, 1939.

ctx.x: No hospital. They had what they called a Piss House where they put them and they quarantined our house so she couldn‟t even get to her children. She had to put food under the gate to them. She was quarantined then and the ones that were babies, really to small to get around, they‟d let her take them to the Piss House. So she wound up in this Piss House with them and she told me what a terrible place it was. They didn‟t give them water. People would drink out the urinal. She said she could see… in the morning she…
